Graduate Research
Pulsed Bipolar Charge Based Ultrafine Particulate Sensor

Fluid Dynamics & Aerosol Instrumentation Technology

Atmose · University of Waterloo · Sep 2025 – Present

Conducting graduate research and industry R&D at Atmose (Edmonton, AB) focused on the development of low cost ultrafine particulate matter sensors. Work combines high-fidelity multiphysics simulation in OpenFOAM with experimental validation to advance next-generation aerosol measurement devices used in air quality and atmospheric science.

  • Developed a coupled multiphysics CFD model in OpenFOAM integrating charged aerosol transport and electrostatics to optimise Faraday cup electrometer geometry for minimal current leakage and maximum signal.
  • Investigated residence time distributions (RTD) in a radioactive neutralizer using CFD and experimental methods; redesigned internal flow geometry to reduce recirculation and improve neutralization performance.
  • First-authored two peer-reviewed manuscripts; co-authored a third, all under review (see Publications below).

Experimental · Heat Transfer · Mechanical Design · In Progress
Aero-Thermal Benchtop Wind Tunnel
Designing and fabricating a suction-type benchtop wind tunnel bridging aerodynamics and heat transfer in a single rig. Tunnel features a bell-mouth, flow straightener, 4:1 contraction, 100 × 100 × 300 mm acrylic test section, and ≤7° diffuser, targeting Re 3,000–25,000. Instrumenting a Ø25 mm heated cylinder (25–50 W cartridge heater, five-point surface TC array at 0°–180°) and integrating a force balance for drag measurement on 3D-printed bluff bodies and airfoils. All signals acquired via NI DAQ; Nu vs. Re data to be validated against Hilpert, Churchill–Bernstein, and Churchill–Chu correlations. Directly applicable to turbine blade cooling and electronics thermal management.

Aerosol Instrumentation · CFD · Machining · MASc Research
Residence Time Distributions in Bipolar Charge Conditioners
Machined the TSI 3077A Kr-85 neutralizer geometry and conducted experiments at 0.3 and 1.5 L/min to measure particle RTD. Developed a 3D OpenFOAM CFD model with turbulent particle dispersion, revealing inlet recirculation zones that create a "memory effect" : RTD mode (1.3 s) is ~22× shorter than plug-flow residence time (28.4 s), with a long tail trapping particles for >100 s. Compared to the Atmose ACC-EL2 Ni-63 charger, which achieved a 3–6× narrower RTD. Demonstrates critical implications for fast-scanning SMPS temporal resolution in transient ultrafine particle measurements.

Aerosol Transport · CFD · Experimental · MASc Research
RTD Effects in Aerosol Sampling Lines
Experimentally characterised residence time distributions (RTD) of aerosol particles in sampling tubes using an atomizer–AAC–fast CPC rig with a 3-way step-change valve. Validated analytical laminar RTD (Poiseuille) solutions across tube geometries and developed an OpenFOAM CFD model for turbulent and complex sampling lines. Demonstrated that transient CPC signals are delayed and broadened by sampling line RTD, with deconvolution identified as a correction path.
OpenFOAMCFD ExperimentalAerosol TransportMATLABPython
✓ CFD validated against analytical model across Re · Manuscript under review
Mechatronics · Robotics · Interdisciplinary Capstone
Assistive Mobility Retrofit for Manual Wheelchairs
Led mechanical design of a retrofittable power-assist drive system for manual wheelchairs, enabling independent mobility for the 60% of long-term users experiencing upper-body strain injuries. Designed telescoping tube frame (17–24 in. adjustable width), revolute motor joint for incline compliance, and quick-release coupler for maintenance. System integrates dual 500 W motors (30 Nm peak, 6 km/h), wheel encoder–based force sensing that detects and proportionally amplifies user input torque, and an STM32 + Arduino motor-controller stack with PWM speed/direction control and an emergency stop, all in a 10 kg, C$800 assembly with a 5-minute setup time.
